subject: Recap + clarifying questions: hosting mode, migration onramp and next steps
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Amit Rao <amit@medialogix.com>, Priya Desai <priya.desai@medialogix.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-18T22:12:00Z
Subject: Quick recap + a few follow-ups on hosting mode and migration onramp

Amit / Priya — thanks again for taking the call today. Short recap and a few clarifying questions so we can scope the right pilot and pricing: 

Recap (what I heard)
- Production needs: low-10s ms token latency target for chat, peak burst ~120 concurrent requests, daily token volume expected ~6–8M tokens initially.
- Compliance: must support VPC peering + customer-managed KMS; PHI-scope prompts in scope for a subset of calls.
- Current stack: sitting behind an external API (AtlasLM) for inference; a legacy on-prem GPU cluster (NVIDIA V100s) used for internal dev workloads and warm-start alignment. Intended to decommission cluster in phases.

Key qualification questions (to confirm)
1) Can you confirm whether PHI will be present in production request bodies or only sanitized metadata?
2) Target cutover window for decommissioning the legacy cluster (approx date or quarter)?
3) Procurement timeline — do you expect an SOW/PO within 6–8 weeks or longer?
4) Any hard latency SLOs (p50/p95) or is 100ms p50 / 250ms p95 acceptable at pilot scale?
5) Are there internal constraints on egress (no public internet from VPC) that would force an on-prem/private-only approach?

Suggested immediate path (subject to your answers):
- Pilot (2–4 weeks): Hosted sandbox (Redwood hosted API) with token limits and logging disabled for PHI traffic — validate prompts, routing, and cost.
- Production ramp: Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) to meet p95 latency and concurrency targets.
- Compliance cutover: Private VPC or on-prem package if procurement/security requires customer-controlled network and HSM-managed keys.

I attached a short migration checklist and hosting comparison to help decide which of the three paths (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) fits each phase — see attachments.

Next steps I propose: you confirm answers to the 5 questions above, and we schedule a 30-minute technical onramp with Soojin to validate network/KMS requirements. If that looks good, we’ll prepare an SOW draft and pilot pricing.

Thanks — Jonas
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0199

Attachments referenced: redwood-migration-checklist-v1.pdf, redwood-hosting-comparison.xlsx
From: Amit Rao <amit@medialogix.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Priya Desai <priya.desai@medialogix.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-19T08:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick recap + a few follow-ups on hosting mode and migration onramp

Thanks Jonas — good summary. Quick answers inline: 

1) PHI: yes, a subset of requests will include PHI (insurance records). We can route those to private-hosted endpoints if needed, but we want the control plane to be Redwood-managed if possible.
2) Legacy cluster: target decommission Q4 2026, but we will cut traffic gradually starting mid-Q3.
3) Procurement: looks like ~6 weeks for an initial PO if the SOW matches our security ask.
4) Latency SLOs: pilot is fine with 120ms p50, 300ms p95. Production target closer to 90ms p50 and 220ms p95 for shortest prompts.
5) Egress: our VPC currently blocks outbound internet; we will need VPC peering or an internal NAT for hosted flows.

We’re interested in validating Hosted API for prompt tuning and then moving to Dedicated for production. If Private VPC is required for PHI, then that would be phase 3.

Next: Priya will coordinate procurement; can we get a technical onramp slot with Soojin next Tue morning? Also please share SOC2 + data handling docs.

—Amit
Amit Rao
Head of ML Platforms, Medialogix
amit@medialogix.com
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Amit Rao <amit@medialogix.com>, Priya Desai <priya.desai@medialogix.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-19T18:28:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick recap + a few follow-ups on hosting mode and migration onramp

Appreciate the quick answers — that helps. Proposed phased plan (consolidated):

Phase A — Pilot (1–3 weeks):
- Hosted sandbox (Redwood hosted API); token limit 1M tokens/2 weeks, no PHI on hosted endpoints — send PHI to isolated sandbox or masked in pilot.
- Goals: validate prompt templates, measure p50/p95 for representative queries, and sanity-check cost cadence.

Phase B — Pre-prod (4–8 weeks):
- Dedicated capacity (reserved capacity) sized for 120 concurrent requests and target p95 budget.
- Enable VPC peering + KMS integration for non-PHI traffic; configure prefix caching.

Phase C — Compliance cutover (quarter 4 target):
- Private VPC or on-prem package, customer-managed KMS/HSM for PHI traffic and audit log export.

Operational and migration notes:
- We can mirror traffic from AtlasLM during the dedicated phase to compare outputs (A/B).
- For the cluster decommission, we recommend a 3-stage rollback plan (smoke tests, gradual shift, rollback window).

Action items
- Medialogix: confirm pilot start date + provide sample prompt set and 500–1000 representative queries (anonymized where needed).
- Redwood: draft SOW and SOC2 evidence pack; schedule 30m onramp with Soojin (tech) + Karthik (solutions).

I attached a first-pass SOW draft and a migration checklist — the checklist highlights the network/KMS items you flagged. If those look ok, I’ll assign a delivery manager and we’ll get procurement looped in.

Thanks,
Jonas
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Amit Rao <amit@medialogix.com>, Priya Desai <priya.desai@medialogix.com>
Date: 2026-07-20T10:02:00Z
Subject: RE: Quick recap + a few follow-ups on hosting mode and migration onramp

Adding a few technical clarifications from the infra/eng side so Medialogix can prep: 

Network & Security- VPC peering is supported; if outbound egress is blocked we can deploy a private endpoint inside your VPC (no public internet egress) and run the control plane with customer-managed KMS for keys. That meets PHI constraints.
- Firewall: we’ll need to open a small set of IP ranges or support a private endpoint; we prefer private endpoint for long-term security.

Performance / Migration- Model compatibility: we’ll map your AtlasLM prompt templates to an equivalent open model family; some prompt engineering required to match outputs deterministically for critical flows.
- KV / cache migration: we can export the relevant KV prefixes from the cluster and import into Redwood prefix cache; expect a 24–48 hour sync window for ~10M keys.
- Batch sizing: start pilot with batch size 8–16; we’ll tune based on observed latency.

Operational tasks (owners)
- Data exports (Medialogix): sample prompt set + sanitization (Priya)
- Network configuration (Medialogix): decide private endpoint vs peering (Amit + infra)
- SOW review (Redwood: Jonas; Solutions: Karthik)

I attached a short tech checklist for the onramp. Happy to discuss items in the Tue slot — I can do Tue 09:00-11:00 PT.

—Soojin
Soojin Lee
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
